messages:
maria (eng-runtime): Quick summary from today's cross-GPU kernel sweep — comparing L4/T4/A10 against A100/H100 with sequence-length aware paths. Uploaded raw CSV to /mnt/perf/crossgpu-sweep.csv :link: 

sam (eng-ml): Nice — what's the headline perf diff?

maria (eng-runtime): TL;DR: for short context (<=128) Turing/Maxwell-class (T4/L4) int8-tile kernels win on latency and cost. For long context (>512) Ampere/Hopper fused-attn fp16 path dominates. Numbers below are p50/p95 token latencies for a single-stream gen on 8k model (batch=1):

maria (eng-runtime): seq=64  — L4 int8_tile32: 11ms / 18ms, A10 int8_opt: 10ms / 16ms, A100 fused_fp16: 14ms / 22ms

maria (eng-runtime): seq=512 — L4 int8: 48ms / 88ms (KV memcpy spikes), A10: 40ms / 72ms, A100 fused_fp16: 26ms / 36ms, H100: 22ms / 31ms

maria (eng-runtime): Observed KV cache behavior: on T4/L4 we hit host<->device memcpy when KV size exceeds ~3.5GB (seq>1024 for 16k context). This causes 2x tail p95 regressions unless we enable streaming-kv or shard KV across devices.

todd (perf): Can you paste the autotune profile you ran? I want to look at kernel switch points.

maria (eng-runtime): Sure — here's the minimal autotune config we prototyped (used in the sweep):

```
# autotune profile (yaml-like pseudoconfig)
device_group:
  - name: turing_family
    devices: [L4, T4]
    preferred_kernels:
      - int8_tile32: {max_seq: 128}
      - int8_tile16: {min_seq: 129, max_seq: 512}
      - fp16_fallback: {min_seq: 513}
  - name: ampere_hopper
    devices: [A10, A100, H100]
    preferred_kernels:
      - fused_attn_fp16: {min_seq: 256}
      - int8_mixed: {min_seq: 64, max_seq: 255}
batching:
  max_batch: 64
  adaptive_window_ms: 6
  min_batch_for_opt: 4
```

sam (eng-ml): That matches intuition. Any regressions flagged?

perf-bot: CI benchmark finished — crossgpu-sweep (master) => regressed +4.3% tail latency on L4 int8 path at seq=512. See: ci/reports/1775/crossgpu-512-l4.html

todd (perf): +4.3% p95 on L4 int8 at seq=512 — likely the memcpy thresholds you mentioned. We should try: 1) lower caching watermarks, 2) prefer fp16 path for seq>=384, or 3) enable KV streaming. Eva, how feasible is streaming-kv on dedicated pools?

eva (eng-infra): Streaming KV is doable but needs changes in our I/O pipeline (pre-post CUDA memcpy overlap). We can deploy a canary to dedicated pools for this week; cost hit uncertain.

maria (eng-runtime): For autotuner I'd like to add a metric-based switch: if KV_allocated_bytes > X then favor fp16_fused irrespective of seq. That avoids memcpy cliff. Also change adaptive_window_ms per device: Turing 4ms, Ampere 8ms.

sam (eng-ml): Also add a model-size hint — 8k vs 16k context affects KV size per token. Autotune should consider model_params * seq as proxy for KV bytes.

todd (perf): Action items: 
- maria: add kv_bytes threshold heuristic to autotuner and re-run sweep (target: remove p95 regression on L4) 
- eva: stand up streaming-kv canary on 1 dedicated pool (L4 nodes) 
- sam: add model-size hint to autotuner proto 

maria (eng-runtime): I'll push a branch with the autotune change and new presets. I'll note the exact thresholds in the PR.

sam (eng-ml): If autotune can't decide, fallback policy should prefer lower-cost kernel unless SLO violation suspected. 

todd (perf): Agreed. Also let's capture raw nvprof traces for seq=512 on L4 — need to inspect memcpy hotspots. Maria can you attach traces to the PR? :thumbsup:

maria (eng-runtime): Yup. Uploading nvprof tarball now. Will tag @todd and @eva in the PR.

perf-bot: benchmark cluster: scheduled rerun for branch/maria/autotune-kv-threshold at 1775012900

maria (eng-runtime): Thanks — will update when rerun finishes.

sam (eng-ml): One more note — quantization quality: int8_tile32 had small logits jitter at seq>256 on A10 in a few prompts. Add fidelity checks to autotune (BLEU/embedding drift) before switching to int8 for longer contexts.

maria (eng-runtime): Good call. Adding a quick eval hook to autotuner.

todd (perf): Great thread. Keeping this short. Ping if you need more perf runs.
